sections.h2: Fast-sale options for a Houston owner
sections.html:
Houston owners choose among a broker listing, a private sale and a cash offer. This is a market unto itself, with 2,397,315 people at the 2025 estimate, and prices can differ sharply between neighboring blocks.

Owners occupy only 42.1% of Houston homes, so landlords, investors and first-time buyers all bid for houses. Cash tends to suit a house with postponed upkeep, storm damage, a tenant or a cloudy title. A listing works best for a house that shows well.

  • Find your deed and survey, and check whether restrictions cover your street.
  • Confirm the appraisal district and taxing units for the address.
  • Collect two written offers, each naming a closing date.

sections.h2: No zoning, but deed restrictions and plats
sections.html:
Houston has no citywide zoning. Voters rejected it, and subdivision deed restrictions steer most construction. Such private restrictions can limit what gets built and how a lot is used. Read yours, then hand the buyer a copy.

The city's planning department requires a plat, a surveyed map of the lot, before building permits. Single-family classification can include a duplex or a garage apartment under 900 square feet unless the deed restrictions forbid it. Houston also reviews plats in an area about five miles beyond its limits, where its permit and inspection rules do not apply.

Plats are filed with the Harris County Clerk's records office after approval. The city's planning site has a map viewer and a Plat Tracker for searching by address.

Houston's midpoint home value was $277,800 over 2020 to 2024, and owners with a mortgage spent $2,240 a month at the median. Because that midpoint spans the whole city, treat it as background and let written offers price your own house.

With rent at $1,361 and owners in a minority of homes, the rental market runs deep. That helps a landlord who is selling, but any seller with a tenant should read the lease and notice rules before saying yes to an offer.

sections.h2: Harris Central Appraisal District and exemptions
sections.html:
Most Houston property is valued for tax by the Harris Central Appraisal District. Owners can file protests, renditions and homestead exemptions on its site, which also has an Exemption Wizard. A deed protection feature lets you register your home with the Harris County Clerk as a guard against deed fraud.

The valuation date is January 1. Homestead notices start near April 1. Your protest is due by May 15, or 30 days after the notice if that is later. If you dislike the board's ruling, district court and binding arbitration are open to you, and so is the State Office of Administrative Hearings once the board value passes $1,000,000. Keep paying whatever part of the tax is not in dispute.

  • Once the exemption is in place, appraised value on a homestead is capped at a 10% rise per year.
  • Heirs absent from the recorded deed must submit an ownership affidavit, the death certificate and a recent utility bill to claim it.
  • A buyer who closes after January 1 can apply for the rest of that year if the seller never filed.

Look at your tax bill to see which district and taxing units cover the parcel.

Buyers and lenders will want answers. Paving and fast runoff have long fed flooding here, and severe floods in 1929 and 1935 led to the Harris County Flood Control District and later the Addicks and Barker reservoirs.

The city says flood mitigation, drainage, water and sewer are outside the Planning Commission's plat review, so a plat does not settle a house's flood risk. Ask the city and the county for flood records on your address, and keep repair records and insurance claims ready for buyers.

Heat, humidity and heavy rain are hard on roofs, siding and air conditioning. A cash buyer will accept storm damage as is, and a documented history helps both sides agree on price.

Plenty of buyers search by neighborhood name. Houston Heights and Pasadena grew as developer-built suburbs in 1892, Bellaire in 1911, West University Place in 1919 and River Oaks in the mid-1920s, and those names still anchor listing descriptions. Several of them are separate municipalities, so check whether your address sits inside Houston or in another city, because that decides who issues permits and which rules apply.

Mention the drive time to downtown, the Texas Medical Center or the ship channel, because the average commute of 27.2 minutes is something buyers weigh. Confirm your school district on the tax bill or with the district before you print it in a listing.

Build a single folder before you list or accept anything. It should hold the deed, any survey, your subdivision's deed restrictions, the newest tax statement and a payoff letter for each loan, plus flood records, repair receipts and insurance claims.

In a market this large buyers compare many houses, and a seller who answers with documents closes faster. Have each bidder state price, closing date, closing-charge split and what happens if the deal collapses, then compare the net after payoffs.

A landlord starts with a written notice to vacate, three days unless the lease names another period. The eviction suit then opens in justice court, with a hearing 10 to 21 days after filing. Appeal to county court is allowed within five days of the judgment, and a writ of possession follows only after six days from final judgment.

Tell every buyer in writing that a tenant lives there and attach the lease. Investors may keep the tenant; a buyer moving in needs the house vacant at closing.

An inheritance tax no longer exists in Texas, since the state repealed it effective September 1, 2015. File probate within four years of a death. The small estate affidavit works only for estates up to $75,000 apart from the homestead.

County clerks record deeds. Heirs should bring the death certificate, any will and a recent tax statement to the first buyer meeting, since the title company will ask who has legal power to sign.

Unpaid taxes leave the January 1 lien on the house, and penalty plus interest start on February 1. If nothing is paid, a taxing unit may sue and have the property auctioned.

Closing a sale first sidesteps all of that. The title company deducts the balance from your proceeds, so request a payoff figure early and compare offers by what remains afterward.

Once you accept, a title company takes over the paperwork. Expect it to search the record, ask each lender for a payoff figure and look at your parcel's tax standing. It then drafts a deed and a settlement statement. Read both before closing day and ask about any line you cannot explain.

At the table a notary witnesses your signature. After the deed is recorded, payoffs and charges are subtracted and the balance goes to you. Cash purchases skip a lender appraisal, so the date holds more easily. Disclose repairs, storm damage or a tenant early, schedule your move so the house is empty at handover, and keep your own copy of every signed page.

faqs.a: Houston covers 640.44 square miles of land and counts 2,397,315 residents at the 2025 estimate. Verify the county and appraisal district for your own address before you rely on any tax figure.
Not citywide. Voters turned it down, but private deed restrictions and the city's plat and permit rules still apply, so read your restrictions.

faqs.q: Can I protest my Houston property value?
faqs.a: Yes. File with the appraisal review board by May 15, or within 30 days of receiving your notice if that is later. The Harris Central Appraisal District site accepts online filing.

faqs.q: Where do I find the plat for my lot?
faqs.a: After approval, plats are filed with the Harris County Clerk's records office. The city's planning site offers a map viewer and a Plat Tracker that search by address.
That is a citywide midpoint from the 2020 to 2024 survey. Your own house needs written offers or an appraisal.
